title: What CPD do Victorian lawyers need to keep their practising certificate?
description: CPD for Victorian solicitors and barristers: 10 points a year, compulsory fields, the 2026 Equality and Wellbeing category, audits and rectification.
shortAnswer: Victorian lawyers holding a practising certificate must complete 10 CPD points in each CPD year from April 1 to March 31, with at least one point in each compulsory field, under the Uniform CPD Rules for solicitors and for barristers. The Victorian Legal Services Board + Commissioner regulates compliance and delegates exemptions and audits to the Law Institute of Victoria for solicitors and the Victorian Bar for barristers. The requirement is 10 points, not 12.
keyTakeaways: Victoria applies the Legal Profession Uniform Continuing Professional Development (Solicitors) Rules 2015 and the matching Barristers Rules 2015, approved as Uniform Rules by the Legal Services Council.

Each practising certificate holder needs 10 points a year with at least one point in ethics and professional responsibility, practice management and business skills, professional (or barristers') skills, and substantive law.
From April 1, 2026 an amendment to the Barristers Rules adds Equality and Wellbeing as a mandatory CPD category for barristers.
The Law Institute of Victoria and the Victorian Bar audit CPD on the regulator's behalf. Audits can reach back over any of the three previous years and evidence is due within 21 days.
Non-compliant lawyers receive a written notice and 90 days to complete a rectification plan; continued refusal can lead to conditions or a fitness to practice referral.
regulator: Victorian Legal Services Board + Commissioner (VLSB+C), with delegated functions to the Law Institute of Victoria (LIV) and the Victorian Bar
appliesTo: Solicitors holding a Victorian practising certificate, including corporate and government lawyers
Barristers holding a Victorian practising certificate
Lawyers moving between the solicitors' and barristers' rules during a CPD year
Law practices and chambers that organize CPD and keep attendance evidence

sections.heading: Who sets and enforces CPD rules for Victorian lawyers?

blocks.text: The rules are national Uniform Rules, but compliance in Victoria is regulated by the Victorian Legal Services Board + Commissioner (VLSB+C). The regulator's [Your CPD obligations](https://lsbc.vic.gov.au/lawyers/practising-law/continuing-professional-development-cpd/your-cpd-obligations) page explains that the CPD Rules "were developed by the national professional associations, the Law Council of Australia and the Australian Bar Association and approved as Uniform Rules by the Legal Services Council", and that the VLSB+C has "delegated some functions associated with CPD compliance to the Law Institute of Victoria (for Solicitors) and the Victorian Bar (for barristers)."

The practical effect is a three-way split. The VLSB+C owns the policy and the renewal declaration; the LIV handles solicitors' exemptions, audits and rectification; and the Victorian Bar does the same for barristers. The regulator's [Continuing Professional Development Policy](https://lsbc.vic.gov.au/resources/continuing-professional-development-policy) is organized in three parts: compliance with the CPD Rules, monitoring compliance, and responding to non-compliance.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects VLSB+C and Legal Services Council publications as at November 2026. Some task briefs and older summaries cite 12 units for Victoria; the VLSB+C states the requirement as 10 points per CPD year.

sections.heading: How many CPD points are required, and in which fields?

blocks.text: Every Victorian practising certificate holder must complete 10 CPD points in each CPD year, including at least one point in each of four fields. The VLSB+C lists them as ethics and professional responsibility; practice management and business skills; professional skills (barristers' skills for barristers); and substantive law, which for barristers includes practice, procedure and evidence.

Each activity must, in the regulator's words, "be of significant intellectual or practical content and be related to the practice of law", be conducted by a suitably qualified person who need not be a lawyer, and extend the lawyer's knowledge and skills relevant to their practice or career development. The VLSB+C does not accredit providers or decide whether a course suits an individual lawyer; that judgment rests with the lawyer.

Barristers have an extra category from April 1, 2026. The Legal Services Council made the Legal Profession Uniform Continuing Professional Development (Barristers) Amendment (Mandatory CPD) Rule 2025, which, according to its [announcement](https://legalservicescouncil.org.au/highlights/new-mandatory-cpd-category-for-barristers.html), includes "Equality and Wellbeing as a mandatory CPD category" so that barristers receive training on discrimination, harassment and wellbeing. The regulator's general CPD page still described four fields as at November 2026, so barristers should confirm the current category list and minimum with the Victorian Bar.

sections.heading: Which CPD activities have limits for Victorian solicitors?

blocks.text: Lectures, seminars, workshops and postgraduate study earn one point per hour with no limit, while writing, presenting, committee work and passive recorded study are capped. The VLSB+C publishes the solicitor limits as follows.

blocks.text: Online interactive material is treated differently from passive recordings. The VLSB+C gives breakout room discussion, chat or question functions, quizzes, tests and polls, and branching scenarios as examples of interaction, and says this type of activity "has no limits". Completing the LIV Accredited Specialisation program counts for a total of 10 points, and a practice management course satisfies all CPD obligations for the year in which it is completed.

sections.heading: How is CPD declared, reduced or exempted in Victoria?

blocks.text: Lawyers declare at practising certificate renewal whether they met their CPD obligations for the year ending March 31. A lawyer who has not met them should attach details of any exemption granted or a rectification plan to the renewal application.

items: **Part-year certificate holders** only need points for the months they held a certificate: 10 for an April start, reducing by one per month to 1 for January, and none for February or March starts. No exemption application is needed in that case.

**Full-year holders** can seek a full or partial exemption for parenting leave or other absence, part-time or reduced hours, disability or illness, or hardship and exceptional circumstances. Applications go to the LIV (solicitors) or the Victorian Bar (barristers) with supporting evidence such as an employer letter, statutory declaration or medical certificate.
**Lawyers returning after a full year without a certificate** do not need to complete CPD or seek an exemption for that year.
**Lawyers switching between roles** during the year should apply the regulator's CPD Policy, because the solicitors' and barristers' rules differ.

blocks.text: Lawyers must keep a record of all CPD activities completed for at least three years. The general principles for retention periods across regulated roles are set out in [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records).

sections.heading: What happens in a Victorian CPD audit or when CPD is missed?

blocks.text: The LIV and the Victorian Bar audit a sample of lawyers every year under delegation, and an audit can relate to any of the three previous CPD years. A selected lawyer is asked to verify compliance within 21 days and supply supporting documents.

The VLSB+C lists acceptable documents as receipts of payment, attendance lists, attendance confirmations, presentation notes, enrollment records and certificates of completion. Where CPD has been missed, the lawyer receives written notice to submit a rectification plan and is given 90 days to complete the planned activities. The regulator states that compliance with the CPD Rules "is a statutory requirement of your entitlement to hold a practicing certificate"; refusal, including failure to complete rectification, may lead to conditions on the certificate or referral for consideration of whether the lawyer is fit and proper to hold one.

blocks.text: Victoria's settings are under a long-running improvement program rather than a rule change. The VLSB+C commissioned an independent review in 2020, and its report, Getting the Point? Review of Continuing Professional Development for Victorian Lawyers, released on November 25, 2020, made 28 recommendations, all of which the regulator accepted.

The review found the system "is not broken" but needs to reflect more contemporary approaches to adult learning. The regulator's stated early focus is better information and guidance and more available, relevant and higher quality ethics CPD, supported by guidance for CPD providers on ethics education released in May 2021. For firms, the direction is clear: plan CPD against real development needs rather than counting hours, an approach described in [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles). Lawyers working across borders can compare the New South Wales administration of the same solicitor rules on the page about [NSW solicitor CPD requirements](/regulations/nsw-solicitor-cpd-requirements).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records which CPD field or category each learning activity addresses, whether it is interactive or passive, and which role it targets, so a chambers or firm can see solicitor and barrister obligations side by side. The resulting records cover the three-year audit lookback and are structured for the documents the LIV and Victorian Bar request.

faqs.q: Is it 10 or 12 CPD points for Victorian lawyers?
faqs.a: It is 10. The Victorian Legal Services Board + Commissioner states that practising certificate holders need 10 CPD points each CPD year, with at least one point in each compulsory field. The 12 figure sometimes quoted does not appear in the regulator's current guidance.

faqs.q: Does the VLSB+C approve CPD courses?
faqs.a: No. The regulator says it does not accredit CPD providers or decide whether courses suit a lawyer's professional needs. Each lawyer is responsible for choosing activities that meet the CPD Rules and for keeping evidence of them.

faqs.q: How far back can a Victorian CPD audit go?
faqs.a: An audit by the LIV or the Victorian Bar can relate to any of the three previous CPD years, which matches the requirement to keep CPD records for at least three years. Selected lawyers have 21 days to verify compliance and provide documents.

faqs.q: Do barristers need Equality and Wellbeing CPD?
faqs.a: Yes, from April 1, 2026. The Legal Services Council amended the Uniform CPD (Barristers) Rules 2015 to add Equality and Wellbeing as a mandatory category, developed by the Australian Bar Association to cover issues such as discrimination, harassment and wellbeing.
